title: JRE 2339 - Luis J. Gomez & Big Jay Oakerson
guestName: Luis J. Gomez & Big Jay Oakerson
guestBio: Luis J. Gomez is a comic, writer, and producer. He co-hosts several podcasts, including “Legion of Skanks,” “The Regz,” “Story Warz,” and “Real Ass Podcast.” You can watch his most recent special, “30 Minutes with Luis J. Gomez,” on YouTube.
tldr: Luis and Jay discuss their comedy careers and the evolution of stand-up comedy in the podcast era
The conversation covers their various podcasts including Legion of Skanks and how they balance multiple shows
They talk about comedy specials and the changing landscape of how comedians release and distribute their content
Discussion of the stand-up comedy community and relationships between comedians in New York and Los Angeles
Luis and Jay share stories from their time performing and building their brands through podcasting
The guests discuss the challenge of maintaining creative output across multiple platforms and projects
recap:
Luis J. Gomez and Big Jay Oakerson brought their considerable chemistry to JRE 2339, diving deep into the world of stand-up comedy, podcasting, and the evolution of how comedians build their careers in the modern era. These two are serious veterans of the comedy scene, having built something real with Legion of Skanks and their other projects, and they weren't shy about discussing the grind of juggling multiple podcasts while still doing stand-up.

The conversation touched on how podcasting has fundamentally changed comedy. Unlike traditional comedians who had to rely on clubs and TV appearances, Luis and Jay have built direct relationships with audiences through their shows. They talked about the reality of doing comedy now versus when they started out, the value of staying independent, and how platforms like YouTube have given them the ability to reach people without traditional gatekeepers. They discussed their various shows and the different audiences each one attracts, emphasizing how the Legion of Skanks community became something bigger than just a podcast.

Luis talked about his recent special and the process of creating comedy content for different platforms. The guys were honest about the amount of work required to maintain their output while also performing live. They discussed the comedy community, the relationships that matter, and how the New York and LA comedy scenes have evolved. There was real talk about the business side of comedy, how to monetize your audience, and what it takes to stay relevant without selling out.

The conversation had the casual, riff-heavy energy you'd expect from these guys. They weren't trying to sound smart or profound. Just two comics who know their lane, have built something genuine, and were there to talk about what they do. It's the kind of episode that works for people who actually care about comedy as a craft and understand the podcast world as a legitimate space for artists to work.
